plain: So honest or solid that it cannot be doubted

webster.text: That cannot be impeached; that cannot be accused; free from stain, guilt or fault; as an unimpeachable reputation.

example.quote: As to the danger from an unimpeachable magistrate he could not regard it as formidable.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, July 19, 1787
